security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, Go import blocks, documentation URLs, and a user-agent string. One setup command is a real external execution risk because it installs Playwright dependencies. Semantic review found anti-bot evasion guidance and misleading safe-risk language, so remediation is required before publication.

remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions for bypassing Cloudflare, Akamai, stealth scripts, proxy rotation, and fingerprint avoidance. Reframe the skill for authorized testing and compliance-friendly automation.
Change safe-risk statements to disclose automation, network access, external installs, and target-site authorization requirements.
Document the installer as optional setup, require user confirmation, pin versions where practical, and explain downloaded dependencies.

content.value_statement: Go teams need browser automation that handles dynamic pages without fragile scripts. This skill guides Playwright Go implementations with contexts, logging, timeouts, and session patterns.
actual_capabilities: Scaffolds Playwright Go initialization with browser launch, context creation, and cleanup.
Recommends Zap logging and explicit timeouts for navigation, clicks, and input actions.
Shows browser-context isolation for separate sessions without relaunching browsers.
Provides examples for human-like typing, mouse movement, and interaction timing.
Outlines cookie-based session save and load patterns for user-implemented storage.
limitations: Requires Playwright drivers and browsers to be installed before generated code can run.
Full browser automation can use significant CPU and memory.
The skill does not solve CAPTCHAs or guarantee access through strict bot defenses.
Stealth and scraping guidance must only be used with authorization from the target site.

use_cases.title: Test Dynamic Web Flows
use_cases.description: Build Go-based browser checks for pages that require JavaScript, user sessions, or complex navigation.

use_cases.title: Collect Authorized Web Data
use_cases.description: Create controlled automation for sites where the team has permission to access and extract data.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Automation Jobs
use_cases.description: Improve flaky Playwright Go workflows with better contexts, timeouts, cleanup, and structured logs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Script
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single page visit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Playwright Go starter script that opens a page, logs actions with Zap, sets explicit timeouts, and closes all resources.

prompt_templates.title: Add Reliable Interactions
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve my Playwright Go flow by replacing fragile waits with locator-based actions, timeouts, error handling, and useful log fields.

prompt_templates.title: Manage Browser Sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Playwright Go session strategy that uses one browser, separate contexts, cookie persistence, and clear cleanup behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned Playwright Go automation job for authorization, resource usage, context pooling, observability, retries, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Create a starter script for visiting a dashboard and checking a heading.
output_examples.output: The response would outline browser startup, context creation, page navigation, heading verification, structured logging, and cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: Improve reliability for a flaky form workflow.
output: Use explicit action timeouts and locator-based waits.
Log each navigation and interaction with context fields.
Close pages and contexts after each workflow.

output_examples.input: Design a session plan for multiple authorized accounts.
output_examples.output: The response would recommend one shared browser, isolated contexts per account, controlled cookie storage, and clear authorization checks.

best_practices: Confirm target-site authorization before generating scraping or automation flows.
Use one browser with separate contexts for independent sessions.
Set explicit timeouts and close pages, contexts, and browsers in all paths.
anti_patterns: Using stealth behavior to bypass access controls or bot protections without permission.
Launching a full browser for every small task.
Relying on default waits, fixed sleeps, or unstructured console output.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Playwright Go browser automation for testing, authorized data collection, and workflow debugging.

faq.question: Does it install Playwright for me?
faq.answer: No. It documents the setup command, but users must approve and run dependency installation themselves.

faq.question: Can it handle JavaScript-heavy sites?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses a real browser through Playwright Go, which can render dynamic client-side pages.

faq.question: Does it solve CAPTCHAs?
faq.answer: No. The skill does not include CAPTCHA solving or guaranteed access through strict bot defenses.

faq.question: Is it safe for scraping any website?
faq.answer: No. Use it only where automation and data access are authorized by the target site.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
